history.content: Reviewed the windows branch. The changes extend the anonymizer patterns to hyphen-encoded home paths, standard Windows `C:\Users\<name>` paths, double-backslash variants, and custom home directories with their MSYS2/WSL `/c/custom_home/<name>/` forms. The review found no correctness problems.

I have successfully added tests in `tests/test_anonymizer.py` to cover the new changes: `test_hyphen_encoded_home_path`, `test_windows_users_path` (including double-backslash scenarios) and `test_wsl_msys2_custom_home_path`, which also verifies that paths from MSYS2/WSL environments using the POSIX structure `/c/custom_home/bob/` are anonymized. I also ran `pytest tests/test_anonymizer.py` to verify the new tests pass.

snapshot.agent_state: The branch adds new anonymizer patterns for Windows, hyphen-encoded and WSL/MSYS2 home paths, and the agent has just finished adding unit tests for them in `tests/test_anonymizer.py`. The anonymizer itself is a list of pattern strings that are applied directly to text as it is read and written, so every pattern is re-evaluated for every string the tool touches. The agent reports that the branch is complete and the tests pass; no performance work has been proposed yet.
